result.notes: tsc --noEmit exits 0. THREE screenshots captured (ws2_a hero / ws2_b ~35% / ws2_c ~65%) but the helmet does NOT appear: documented headless-GPU limitation, NOT a code failure. Headless chromium SwiftShader -> getGPUTier() in lib/usePerfTier.ts classifies renderer as 'low' -> SceneContainer renders SvgCoreFallback and the ambient WebGL Canvas never mounts (diagnostic: 0 canvas elements, 0 GLB requests). GLB serves HTTP 200 (3.77MB). On a real GPU the canvas mounts and the helmet travels/lands per section. The fallback behaving this way also confirms the gating guardrail is intact. NEEDS real-GPU browser verification by the user.
result.summary: Implemented WS2 traveling 3D model. Extended ScenePose with pos[x,y,z]/rot[x,y,z]/scale per section + matching ScenePoseTarget fields (pos/rot as Vector3, scale number), makePoseTarget, and component-wise lerp in samplePose. Per-section waypoints trace hero(up/right near sun) -> about(close/left) -> skills(orbit right) -> projects(recede high/back) -> experience(orbit left) -> contact(centred). Created TravelerModel.tsx: useGLTF('/models/DamagedHelmet.glb') + preload, clones scene, each frame reads sceneStore.progress + samplePose and THREE.MathUtils.damp's group position/rotation/scale toward target (same pattern as CameraController, slightly slower so it trails the camera) + subtle sin idle bob + slow Y spin; drei Environment+Lightformers light the PBR helmet. Mounted in Scene.tsx beside ParticleField inside the existing single Suspense. No second pause mechanism: model shares the canvas whose frameloop flips to 'never' on portfolio:bg-pause (one canvas active at a time). SceneContainer/SvgCoreFallback gating intact.
